source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's SAT1 campus in San Antonio publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 110,000 square feet, and that 9 MW is the only power figure attached to the site.

The certifications are the more specific signal. PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942 qualify the campus for payment, health, federal and audited workloads. They say nothing about which tenants actually occupy it, and the operator publishes no tenant roster, no rack count and no GPU count. Any conversion from 9 MW to racks or accelerators is arithmetic on an assumption, not a disclosed specification.

Texas holds 137 mapped facilities, of which 19 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 475.41 MW. SAT1 ranks 14th in the state by published megawatts. That rank sits inside a small disclosed subset, not inside the state's full buildout, because most Texas facilities disclose nothing at all.

What the data does not cover is expansion. The suitability score of 56 lists announced expansion as missing, so nothing here indicates whether 9 MW is the campus's ceiling or a current stage. For AI specifically, the binding question is how much power the site can actually draw, and on the published record that number is 9 MW.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
